column1: # Campaign class of each node for scripts/correctness_matrix.py (the class table of the
# cross-architecture correctness campaign). Tab-separated, one row per host:
#   host     short host name (hostname -s; a JSON "host" FQDN is cut at the first dot),
#            or "-" for a class with no fixed node
#   class    campaign class; the matrix rows follow the order of first appearance here
#   arch     arch.class the node's JSON must report (intel, amd, grace); a mismatch is a
#            blocking deviation, so a host mapped to the wrong class cannot pass silently
# A class may list several hosts; their results merge (worst status wins). milan and a100 run
# on the same node, so they are one class. milan-cpu has no fixed node (the operator picks an
# idle GPU-less Milan node): assign it on the command line with --class-map HOST=milan-cpu,
# which also adds or overrides any other host. Expectations: correctness_expected.tsv.
